$comment: Documented @pyreon/zero features with NO real-build test (e2e spec or verify-modes cell). This list is a RATCHET: scripts/check-zero-feature-coverage.ts fails if it grows relative to origin/main. To remove an entry, add a real-build test and a registry entry in scripts/zero-feature-coverage.ts. Never add one to make the gate pass.

uncovered.Single-instance contract: unit-tested only (duplicate-instance sentinel); no built app loads two copies
uncovered.SPA apps ship without hydration code: no cell asserts the hydration runtime is ABSENT from a pure-SPA client bundle
uncovered.Route Groups: no example uses a (group)/_layout directory in a built app
uncovered.Virtual Modules: exercised implicitly by every build; no test imports virtual:zero/* from user code
uncovered.Typed routes: type-level unit tests only; no built example typechecks RouterLink against generated route types
uncovered.Streaming by default (`mode: 'ssr'`): no e2e asserts an SSR page response is chunked / streamed
uncovered.Delivery polish (SSG toggles): no verify-modes cell toggles these SSG options
uncovered.ISR: tag-based invalidation + filesystem: revalidateTag and createFsStore have no built-server test
uncovered.`<Link>` external links: unit-tested only; no e2e asserts target/rel on a built page
uncovered.Composing them — `@pyreon/zero/middlewar: no built app composes the shipped middlewares (rate limit, CORS, security headers)
uncovered.CSP Nonce: no built-server test asserts the nonce reaches inline scripts
uncovered.Using a backend proxy in dev: integration test runs a dev server in vitest, not an e2e spec
uncovered.Server Actions: no example, e2e spec or verify-modes cell uses defineAction (audit WP5)
uncovered.Image Processing: no cell asserts the image plugin's generated variants
uncovered.Favicons: no cell asserts generated favicon files
uncovered.Social-Share Images (og:image): no cell asserts generated og:image files
uncovered.Fail the build on a missing public var —: no cell asserts a failing build
uncovered.Testing Utilities: a test-helper API; exercised by unit tests, which is its real-world use
